full_judgment: 8. This impugned order was issued on 3.10.87 from the office of the Deputy Commissioner. Thereafter, the defendant No. 1 made certain construction on his land and brought the machineries for the cinema hall. All these things are on record. Mr. Moqbul Ahmed has drawn our attention to Article 14 of the Limitation Act. He submits that this is a Government order under Cinematograph Rules and from the date of order within one year the suit ought to have been filed. But the present suit was filed long after one year and that is why the suit is barred by limitation. It is in evidence that after receipt of the order from the Deputy Commissioner the defendant No. 1 made construction on the proposed place and thereafter he brought his machineries there. So, it was very much within the knowledge of the plaintiffs that the defendant No. 1 was making construction of cinema hall and brought the machineries there. Though it was within the knowledge of the plaintiffs, they instituted the suit after about two years. So, in our view, this present suit is hit by Article 14 of the Limitation Act inasmuch as suit was not filed within one year from the date of the issuance of the No-Objection Certificate. Since the construction was made and machineries were brought, it is apparent that this was within the knowledge of the plaintiffs. But they did not take steps in the matter for filing any suit. Further, after obtaining the certificate the defendant No. 1 made certain construction and brought his machineries. It appears that he spent about Taka 25 lakh in this project for over these two years in connection with establishment of the cinema hall. At this stage such no-objection certificate cannot be declared illegal inasmuch as in the meantime some right has been accrued in favour of the defendant No. 1 and further the defendant No. 1 will suffer irreparable loss and injury for no fault of his own.
